newsitem.title: USA: U.S. backs Hong Kong protests.
newsitem.headline: U.S. backs Hong Kong protests.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday backed the right of Hong Kong's pro-democracy activists to demonstrate when the territory switches from British rule on July 1 despite rising fears the first day under China will turn nasty.

"You have Hong Kong. You have the democratic activists there. You have the government there. And you have China, which will assume control of Hong Kong very shortly. They need to work out all of these issues," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
"The United States supports the right of people to peacefully assemble and protest government policies in our own country and in countries around the world," he said.
Fears are rising in Hong Kong that a "symbolic gesture" by the Democratic Party early on the territory's first day under China will turn nasty despite the Democrats' commitment to peaceful protest.
Hong Kong's largest party says it will occupy the chamber of parliament, expressing anger at the elected assembly's death as a globally-televised handover ceremony and gala takes place nearby.

Asked about these plans, Burns said: "When we talk about the need to preserve Hong Kong's way of life, we mean exactly this -- democratic freedoms that the people of Hong Kong have and should continue to have after July 1. That's our hope.

"And that is the fundamental reason why Secretary (of State Madeleine) Albright is going to Hong Kong -- to stand up and to say we hope that this transfer does not diminish the rights of people to enjoy a democratic way of life," he added.
Albright has accepted an invitation to attend the ceremonies surrounding the handover. She will be in Hong Kong from June 29 to July 1.

Burns said Albright did not have any plans to meet with the demonstrators but would meet a "cross-section" of the Hong Kong population -- including democracy advocates -- as well as Chinese leaders who will be in the territory for the handover.
